title: What to Remember, What to Reveal: Privacy-Aware Memory for Conversational Agents
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: A sensitive-data-aware system separates private values at write time, stores them in isolated partitions, and releases them only with consent at query time.
layout: 3 stacked horizontal bands, left-to-right flow, dashed cross-band links, legend bottom-right
description: A wide diagram split into three colored horizontal bands. The top blue band, 'Privacy-Aware Memory Writing Pipeline', runs left to right from a User Interaction chat icon through an agent and an information extraction box. Extraction splits into private and non-private information, then privacy sanitization, privacy-sanitized information, exact private information, and privacy mapping construction (chain-link icon). The middle green band, 'Partitioned Memory Storage Layer', has three containers holding database cylinders: a sanitized searchable layer (vector and graph stores), a privacy mapping layer (lock icon), and a protected private storage (lock icon). The bottom lavender band, 'Privacy-Aware Query-Time Reasoning Pipeline', goes from User Query through an agent and query analysis to a 'Privacy Needed?' diamond. 'No' leads to ordinary retrieval. 'Yes' leads to a consent check diamond, then authorization-gated retrieval or denial. All paths feed retrieved context, a response generator and the agent response. Orange dashed lines link storage to retrieval, and a legend sits at the bottom right.
caption: Overview of the privacy-aware conversational agent framework. The system contains three stages: privacy-aware memory writing, partitioned memory storage, and query-time privacy-aware reasoning. Private values are sanitized before storage and are only hydrated at inference time when the task requires them and the user grants consent.
abstract: Long-term memory enables personalized conversational agents to retain user information across sessions. However, existing memory architectures primarily optimize for utility while neglecting the risks of unnecessarily storing and reusing private attributes such as personally identifiable information (PII). Addressing privacy risks in personalized memory is challenging because simply removing sensitive values can undermine system utility. Therefore, privacy protection for memory agents should govern the full life cycle of sensitive values rather than only sanitizing individual records. To address this gap, we introduce Sanitized Privacy-Mapped Memory (SP-Mem), a privacy-aware memory architecture that decouples memory utility from exact private-value exposure. SP-Mem provides a full life-cycle privacy design that identifies and separates sensitive information from raw user inputs, stores sanitized content and exact private values in isolated structures, and selectively retrieves private values based on task requirements and user consent. We further introduce a privacy-aware memory benchmark that jointly evaluates response quality, privacy behavior, and inference cost. Extensive experiments across multiple LLM-based agents show that SP-Mem achieves stronger personalization while reducing unnecessary privacy exposure. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Jensassss/SP-Mem.
